features.name: Valhalla
features.description: Valhalla is Callisto's signature landmark and one of the Solar System's largest known impact structures. A bright central zone is surrounded by an enormous pattern of concentric fractures where Callisto's cold, icy crust rang outward after an ancient collision.

details.label: IAU diameter
details.value: About 3,000 km for the named ringed feature

details.label: Central bright zone
details.value: Roughly 600 km across in Galileo-era imaging

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Bright bullseye-like terrain near 15-17 degrees north, about 122-124 degrees east in the app view

details.label: Science value
details.value: The rings show how impact energy spread through a rigid ice shell without the global resurfacing seen on Europa or Ganymede.

features.name: Asgard
features.description: Asgard is Callisto's second-largest named multi-ring basin. Its broad pale interior and surrounding arcs sit in the northern hemisphere, preserving a second example of the way major impacts fractured Callisto's ice-rich crust.

details.label: IAU diameter
details.value: About 1,400 km

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Large pale ringed terrain near 32 degrees north, 40 degrees east in the app view

details.label: Nearby context
details.value: Utgard lies close to Asgard and partly overlaps the same complex high-latitude terrain.

details.label: Science value
details.value: Asgard helps compare different generations of basin formation on a world with very little later geologic erasure.

features.name: Adlinda
features.description: Adlinda is a large southern multi-ring basin, smaller than Valhalla and Asgard but still vast on a moon only about 4,821 km wide. Its subdued arcs and degraded terrain show how ancient impacts can remain readable even after billions of years of micrometeorite gardening and slow ice relaxation.

details.label: IAU diameter
details.value: About 840 km

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Southern hemisphere ringed terrain near 49 degrees south, 144 degrees east in the app view

details.label: Why it matters
details.value: Adlinda extends the basin story away from the bright Valhalla hemisphere and helps show that giant impacts scarred Callisto globally.

features.name: Utgard
features.description: Utgard is a large ringed feature near Asgard, making the region one of Callisto's richest impact-basin neighborhoods. Its overlap with older and younger markings gives the surface a layered, palimpsest-like appearance.

details.label: IAU diameter
details.value: About 610 km

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Northern high-latitude ringed feature close to Asgard, near 45 degrees north, 46 degrees east in the app view

details.label: Reading the terrain
details.value: The crowded basin field helps students see how impacts of different ages overlap on an old, inactive surface.

features.name: Kol Facula
features.description: Kol Facula is Callisto's single named facula, a bright spot that stands out against the moon's darker, heavily cratered terrain. It gives the feature set a useful visual target beyond craters, ring basins, and crater chains.

details.label: IAU diameter
details.value: About 390 km

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Bright low-latitude patch near 5 degrees north, 103 degrees west in the app view

details.label: Naming origin
details.value: Named for Kol, an Icelandic frost or storm giant.

features.name: Bran
features.description: Bran is a prominent mid-sized crater in Callisto's southern hemisphere. Its cleaner circular outline contrasts with the battered background terrain and helps anchor the anti-Jovian side of the texture with a recognizable named impact.

details.label: IAU diameter
details.value: About 78 km

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Southern crater near 24 degrees south, 26 degrees west in the app view

details.label: Naming origin
details.value: Named from Celtic tradition for an omnipotent god who watched over people.

features.name: Lofn
features.description: Lofn is one of Callisto's large named craters, positioned in the far southern terrain near the Adlinda basin. Its broad impact scar is a useful comparison point for basin-scale impacts because it is large enough to reshape regional terrain but not large enough to create Valhalla-style global rings.

details.label: IAU diameter
details.value: About 200 km

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Southern crater near 57 degrees south, 158 degrees east in the app view

details.label: Science value
details.value: Large craters like Lofn help reveal how Callisto's ice-rich crust slowly relaxes while still preserving a very old impact record.

features.name: Har
features.description: Har is a low-latitude crater near Callisto's anti-meridian in the app view. Its position makes it a helpful reference point for checking that source Gazetteer longitudes have been remapped onto the displayed texture.

details.label: IAU diameter
details.value: About 52 km

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Small equatorial crater near 4 degrees south, 178 degrees west in the app view

details.label: Coordinate note
details.value: IAU source longitude 358 degrees west remaps to 178 degrees west for this displayed texture.

features.name: Heimdall
features.description: Heimdall is a large high-southern crater close to the 0-degree meridian. It is useful for showing how named Callisto craters appear at very different scales, from small circular bowls to broad, softened impact structures hundreds of kilometers wide.

details.label: IAU diameter
details.value: About 210 km

details.label: Map cue
details.value: High-southern crater near 64 degrees south, 177 degrees west in the app view

details.label: Correction note
details.value: This entry uses the IAU Gazetteer location; the previous north-polar placement was not aligned to the map.

features.name: Debegey
features.description: Debegey is Callisto's third-largest named crater, a broad impact structure in the northern low latitudes. Its size places it between the giant softened craters and the more common smaller bowls scattered across the ancient surface.

details.label: IAU diameter
details.value: About 125 km

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Northern low-latitude crater near 10 degrees north, 14 degrees east in the app view

details.label: Naming origin
details.value: Named for Debegey, a Yukaghir mythological hero.

features.name: Gloi
features.description: Gloi is one of Callisto's largest named craters and anchors the northern hemisphere away from the Valhalla and Asgard basin fields.

details.label: IAU diameter
details.value: About 115.3 km

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Northern crater near 49 degrees north, 65 degrees west in the app view

details.label: Source longitude
details.value: IAU source longitude 245 degrees west, equivalent to 115 degrees east before the texture-display remap.

features.name: Nori
features.description: Nori completes the top-five largest named crater set for Callisto. It lies in the northern hemisphere near the anti-meridian in the app view.

details.label: IAU diameter
details.value: About 114 km

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Northern crater near 45 degrees north, 164 degrees west in the app view

details.label: Source longitude
details.value: IAU source longitude 343.6 degrees west, equivalent to 16.4 degrees east before the texture-display remap.

features.name: Eikin Catena
features.description: Eikin Catena is a low-latitude crater chain. It helps round out Callisto's named catenae set and gives a clear example of how a fragmented impactor can leave a long stitched path of craters.

details.label: IAU length/diameter measure
details.value: About 223 km

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Low-latitude crater chain near 9 degrees south, 165 degrees east in the app view

details.label: Source longitude
details.value: IAU source longitude 15.5 degrees west.

features.name: Fimbulthul Catena
features.description: Fimbulthul Catena is a long crater chain crossing the Valhalla-side hemisphere. Its scale makes it one of the more useful chain features for visual checking against the global texture.

details.label: IAU length/diameter measure
details.value: About 287 km

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Low northern crater chain near 8 degrees north, 115 degrees east in the app view

details.label: Source longitude
details.value: IAU source longitude 64.8 degrees west.

features.name: Geirvimul Catena
features.description: Geirvimul Catena is a northern crater chain close to the 0-degree meridian. It adds a compact chain target outside the larger Valhalla and Asgard basin fields.

details.label: IAU length/diameter measure
details.value: About 113 km

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Northern crater chain near 49 degrees north, 167 degrees west in the app view

details.label: Source longitude
details.value: IAU source longitude 347.2 degrees west.

features.name: Gipul Catena
features.description: Gipul Catena is a long chain of craters in Callisto's northern hemisphere. Catenae on icy moons are often linked to fragmented impactors, where a disrupted comet or asteroid strikes in a sequence and leaves a dotted line across the surface.

details.label: IAU length/diameter measure
details.value: About 641 km

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Northern crater chain arcing near 69 degrees north, 126 degrees east in the app view

details.label: Science value
details.value: Crater chains connect Callisto to the broader Jovian system, where Jupiter's gravity can tear passing bodies into fragments before impact.

features.name: Gomul Catena
features.description: Gomul Catena is another named crater chain on Callisto, shorter than Gipul Catena but easier to connect visually with the Valhalla hemisphere. Its beads of impact pits preserve a record of a body arriving as multiple fragments rather than a single projectile.

details.label: IAU length/diameter measure
details.value: About 343 km

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Northern-midlatitude crater chain near 36 degrees north, 133 degrees east in the app view

details.label: Classroom cue
details.value: Compare this dotted impact trail with single craters and ringed basins to see three different impact outcomes on one moon.

features.name: Gunntro Catena
features.description: Gunntro Catena is a southern crater chain near the 0-degree meridian. It balances the northern catenae by showing that fragmented-impact trails are not confined to one hemisphere.

details.label: IAU length/diameter measure
details.value: About 149 km

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Southern crater chain near 20 degrees south, 163 degrees west in the app view

details.label: Source longitude
details.value: IAU source longitude 343.1 degrees west.

features.name: Sid Catena
features.description: Sid Catena is a shorter northern crater chain. Its inclusion completes the named Callisto catenae set from the geological features list for visual review.

details.label: IAU length/diameter measure
details.value: About 81 km

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Northern crater chain near 49 degrees north, 76 degrees east in the app view

details.label: Source longitude
details.value: IAU source longitude 103.9 degrees west.

features.name: Svol Catena
features.description: Svol Catena is a low northern crater chain near the Valhalla side of Callisto. Together with Gipul and Gomul, it makes crater chains easier to compare against large ringed structures in the same broad hemisphere.

details.label: IAU length/diameter measure
details.value: About 161 km

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Low northern crater chain near 11 degrees north, 143 degrees east in the app view

details.label: Source longitude
details.value: IAU source longitude 37.2 degrees west.

features.name: North Polar Region
features.description: Callisto's north polar region is a densely cratered ancient landscape that has remained largely geologically quiet for billions of years. Unlike Io, Europa, and Ganymede, Callisto is not locked in the same strong orbital resonance, so Jupiter's tides have not continually refreshed its surface.

details.label: Map cue
details.value: High northern cratered terrain above 80 degrees north

details.label: Why it matters
details.value: The polar regions help show that Callisto's old impact record is global, not limited to the famous basin hemisphere.

details.label: Exploration note
details.value: Callisto's distance from Jupiter keeps it outside the most intense radiation zones around the planet.

features.name: South Polar Region
features.description: Callisto's south polar region continues the moon's ancient cratered character into high southern latitudes. Its terrain is a reminder that Callisto is a fossilized record of early outer Solar System bombardment, with far less resurfacing than the inner Galilean moons.

details.label: Map cue
details.value: High southern cratered terrain below 80 degrees south

details.label: Exploration note
details.value: Callisto has been discussed as a potential future staging point because it offers solid terrain with a much lower radiation burden than Io or Europa.

details.label: Science value
details.value: Comparing both poles with Valhalla and Asgard helps separate global crater saturation from local basin structure.
